title: O God! the Darkness Roll Away
description: O God! the Darkness Roll Away in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 172, “Thy Kingdom Come!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God! the dark-ness roll a-way Which clouds the hu-man soul, And let the bright, the per-fect day, Speed on-ward to its goal.

lines: O God! the darkness roll away
And let the bright, the perfect day,
And war no longer raise its cry,
Let faith, and hope, and charity,
Go forth through all the earth;
And man, in heavenly bearing, be
Yea, let Thy glorious kingdom come
And make this world a portal meet

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
